# Psalm 142 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** A contemplative prayer of David, written when he was hiding in a cave. I cry out to the LORD at the top of my voice; I beg the LORD for mercy out loud.

**2** I pour out all my complaints in front of him; I lay all my troubles before him.

**3** When I'm about to collapse, you know the path I'm on. They've hidden a trap right where I walk.

**4** Look around me — no one even notices me. I have nowhere to run. Not a single person cares what happens to me.

**5** I cry out to you, LORD! I say, 'You are my only safe place — everything I have in this world.'

**6** Pay attention to my cry — I'm completely desperate! Rescue me from my pursuers — they're stronger than I am!

**7** Free me from this prison so I can praise your name! The righteous will gather around me when you show me your generosity.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **142:4**: 'No one even notices me. I have nowhere to run. Nobody cares.' Three devastating statements in a row. This is what total isolation feels like — and the psalm doesn't pretend it away. It just redirects the cry to God.

- **142:7**: 'Free me from this prison so I can praise your name' — the motivation for rescue isn't comfort but worship. The psalmist's deepest desire isn't escape but thanksgiving.

— PNEUMA
